data.title: Haze from Indonesian fires spreading again

data.title: 5 EU countries aim to send rejected migrants to 'return hub' by 2027
data.description: COPENHAGEN - Five EU countries are seeking a deal with a country outside the bloc to host a "return hub" for migrants whose asylum applications have been rejected, with a targeted start date of January 1, a Danish minister said Friday.

data.title: More than 120 killed in Yemen's worst clashes in years: sources
data.description: SANAA - A major offensive by Yemen's Houthis to seize control of the gateway to the Red Sea has left more than 120 people dead, sources told AFP Friday, the country's deadliest clashes in years.

data.title: Call to ‘turn off the tap’ to Ukraine sparks furore in France
data.description: PARIS - A senior official in French presidential contender Marine Le Pen’s far-right party sparked a furore on Friday with a comment that France would “turn off the tap” to Ukraine if it came to power.

data.title: Voting begins in crucial US midterm elections
data.description: WASHINGTON - Voting in the US midterm elections effectively began Friday as North Carolina became the first state to send out mail ballots for contests expected to threaten President Donald Trump’s Republican control of Congress.

data.title: France to abandon ‘distorted’ Mercator map projection
data.description: PARIS - The French foreign ministry on Friday said it plans to abandon using maps with the traditional Mercator projection of the world, backing a push by Africa to give the continent a more realistic geographical representation.

data.title: Swiss far-right extremists go on trial amid protests
data.description: ZURICH - Six members of the Swiss far-right Junge Tat movement went on trial in Zurich on Friday on charges including inciting hatred in disrupting LGBTQ events, as protesters rallied outside calling for their conviction.

data.title: Rubio to visit Trump-friendly allies in South America
data.description: WASHINGTON - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel next week to Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, three Latin American nations whose leaders are close to President Donald Trump, the State Department said Friday.

data.title: Weather and war push up world food prices
data.description: PARIS - Food price inflation accelerated in August as drought and conflicts impacted commodity markets, with sugar prices hitting their highest level in more than a year, UN data showed on Friday.

data.title: Optimised urinals and buried underwear at 2026 Ig Nobels
data.description: ZURICH - Underwear buried to test soil quality and urinals scientifically designed to prevent splashing were among the projects honoured as the Ig Nobel prizes again put a spotlight on the quirky side of science.

data.title: Nepal’s ‘Himalayan tsunami’: what we know
data.description: KATHMANDU - Nepal is still reeling from a deadly Himalayan glacial mountain collapse on the border with China that has killed more than 1,300 people and left upwards of 5,600 missing in both countries.

data.title: Farage's Reform UK meets as new donation scandal hits
data.description: BIRMINGHAM (UNITED KINGDOM) — British hard-right leader Nigel Farage's Reform UK party gathered for its annual conference on Friday engulfed by a fresh scandal over allegations it flouted donations rules.

data.title: Zelensky slams his security services for 'unacceptable' shootout
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has slammed his security services after a shootout between rival agencies in Kyiv this week, saying he planned dismissals of high-ranking officials.

data.title: China arrests 52 Singaporeans for alleged pyramid scheme activities
data.description: SINGAPORE — Chinese ⁠authorities ⁠haves arrested 52 Singaporeans ​in Guangxi, China, after a law enforcement operation ​against pyramid scheme activities ‌and related offences, Singapore's second minister for foreign affairs said on Friday.

data.title: Japanese scientist posthumously wins Ig Nobel prize for nose-blowing study
data.description: The late Japanese researcher Tokuji Unno won this year's Ig Nobel Prize in medicine on Thursday for his study on how to blow one's nose.

data.title: Tanker captain arrested over cargo ship sinking off Istanbul
data.description: ISTANBUL - The captain of an oil tanker that collided with a cargo ship which sank off Istanbul leaving 10 missing has been arrested along with his third-in-command on charges of negligent homicide, prosecutors in Turkey said Friday.

data.title: UK asserts 'unshakeable' Falklands commitment after Milei presses claim
data.description: BUENOS AIRES (ARGENTINA) - Britain insisted on Friday that the Falkland Islands "are British" after Argentine President Javier Milei said the "winds of change" favored his country's claim to the archipelago, citing Washington's readiness to review its neutrality in the dispute.

data.title: German AfD's love for Simson mopeds dismays Jewish family behind brand
data.description: BERLIN - German far-right AfD politicians have shown a fondness for riding vintage Simson scooters that are icons of the former communist East Germany -- much to the dismay of the Jewish family whose name adorns the machines.

data.title: Two trapped tunnel workers rescued in Nepal 'miracle'
data.description: KATHMANDU (NEPAL) - Two hydropower workers were pulled alive from a tunnel buried by debris in Nepal on Friday, a rare ray of hope on the tenth day of rescue efforts after catastrophic Himalayan flooding.

data.title: Arsenal brace for Chelsea test as Spurs seek spark
data.description: LONDON - Something has to give when Arsenal host Chelsea in the Premier League this weekend, with both teams putting their 100 percent records on the line, while Tottenham are desperate to stop the rot.

data.title: Westerners test their mettle at World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan
data.description: CHOLPON-ATA (KYRGYZSTAN) - From wrestling horseback to battling for control of a headless goat, Central Asia's unique sports have been in the spotlight this week as Kyrgyzstan hosts the World Nomad Games, a biannual competition dedicated to nomadic traditions.

data.title: Chile protesters see shades of Pinochet in new security plan
data.description: SANTIAGO (CHILE) - Hundreds of Chilean protesters comparing right-wing President Jose Antonio Kast's security policies with those of late dictator Augusto Pinochet clashed with police in Santiago on Thursday.

data.title: 'Wallace & Gromit' creators turn 50 with spook-tacular Shaun yarn
data.description: BRISTOL (UNITED KINGDOM) - Crochet hook in hand, the animator slightly raises the eyelid of a clay model sheep in a filmmaking technique as old as cinema, perfected over five decades by Aardman Animations.

data.title: Hugging Face, the French start-up that became AI's warehouse
data.description: NEW YORK - Hugging Face, the artificial intelligence platform US chip giant Nvidia is buying for $12.9 billion, is a French success story -- founded by three Frenchmen and incubated in Paris -- even if its headquarters and many of its investors are American.

data.title: How El Nino is choking the Panama Canal
data.description: PANAMA CITY - The Panama Canal will restrict the number of vessels transiting the crucial waterway from Friday for the second time ever due to drought caused by the El Nino climate phenomenon.

data.title: Zelensky hopes to host US envoys in Kyiv in 'coming days'
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Thursday he hoped to host US President Donald Trump's envoys in Kyiv in the coming days to resume efforts to end the Russian invasion.

data.title: Ahead of elections, Israel tests West's patience on West Bank violence
data.description: JERUSALEM - Israel's ties with many Western allies were already fraught over its conduct in the Gaza war, but the worsening situation in the occupied West Bank has seen relations nosedive before close-fought October elections.

data.title: Volkswagen says cutting 100,000 jobs by end of decade
data.description: FRANKFURT (GERMANY) - German car giant Volkswagen said Thursday that management and unions had agreed to cut a total of 100,000 jobs by the end of the decade, the biggest-ever restructuring in the global auto industry.

data.title: Russia slaps curfew on charity director over army criticism
data.description: MOSCOW - A Russian court on Thursday imposed a curfew and communications blackout on the head of a children's hospice accused of spreading "false information" about the army, as Moscow cracks down on critics of its Ukraine offensive.
